subject: general
question: On which day do we celebrate the festival of 'Holi' according to the Hindu calendar?

options.text: A day after the full moon

solution:
The correct answer is __**A day after the full moon**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Holi **is typically celebrated at the end of winter, on the day after the full moon in the **Hindu month of Phalguna, which usually falls in late February or early March.**
 
• The night before Holi is known as **Holika Dahan or Choti Holi, during which bonfires are lit to signify the burning of the evil Holika.**
 
• The next day, which is the **main day of Holi celebrations, is often called Dhulandi or Rangwali Holi, where people play with colours and water.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__**Important festival of India**__

 
• **Diwali** - It is a festival of lights and one of the biggest festivals in India.
 
• **Dussera** - It is the story of the **triumph of Rama, an avatar of Vishnu, over the 10-headed demon king Ravana**. It is celebrated as the symbol of the triumph of good over evil.
